From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Mar 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: ACME POC - next steps and success criteria

Thanks for the demo call today  really appreciate the context on ACME's search and summarization use cases. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're all aligned: 

High-level success criteria (proposed)
- Precision on relevance: >= 85% of returned passages match user intent on our test set
- Summarization fidelity: ROUGE-L / manual pass rate target >= 80%
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile < 350ms for single-request queries in production-like config
- Stability: no more than 1% failure/jitter in 48-hour shadow run

Proposed evaluation plan
1) Offline eval (2 weeks): run 3 representative datasets you provide + synthetic edge cases. We'll run both automated metrics and blinded human grading.
2) Online shadow (3 weeks): low-traffic shadowing on your staging environment with Canary routing. Monitor latency/cost/quality and rollback triggers.

Ownership & timeline- ACME provides datasets & success criteria confirmation by Fri 3/26- Redwood: build offline eval harness (owner: Rachel Kim) by 4/2; run offline eval 4/34/16- Redwood: shadow rollout (owner: Dylan Brooks) 4/195/9 with daily check-ins

Next steps- Can you confirm the datasets you plan to share and whether the proposed success criteria look right?- If yes, we'll send the formal eval rubric and schedule (attachment) and lock a kickoff on your calendar.

Attachments: Acme_POC_Success_Criteria.xlsx (proposed), Redwood_Eval_Rubric.pdf (draft)

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 23 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: ACME POC - eval methodology suggestion

Marissa/Rachel  quick internal note before we send the rubric back to ACME. My suggested approach: 

1) Offline eval (owner: Rachel)- Automated metrics: relevance precision@k, MRR, ROUGE-L for summaries- Blind human grading: 3-point scale (0 = incorrect/unsafe, 1 = partially correct, 2 = correct/high-quality). Each sample graded by 3 raters; use majority/average to decide pass rate.- Failure modes to flag: hallucinations, missing context, PII exposure, repeated truncation.

2) Shadow run (owner: Dylan)- Live traffic mirroring for 3 weeks at 510% of traffic in staging. Collect model outputs and system metrics (latency/cost/errors).- Signal types: system telemetry, NPS-style samping from internal reviewers, basic user-feedback checkbox if ACME wants (opt-in).- Guardrails: auto-fallback to baseline model if error rate > 1% or 95p latency > 450ms for > 30m window.

Grading rubric (high-level)- Quality score per request: combination of automated metric + human grade; define pass if quality score >= 0.75- Safety/Compliance: binary fail if PII exposed or policy violation detected

I'll draft a one-page rubric that maps to the metrics above  Rachel can finalize the offline harness requirements. Once we agree, Marissa can send to ACME.

Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

- Shadow run (4/195/9): Dylan will own live mirroring and rollout controls (we'll provide a runbook with rollback triggers).
- Acceptance criteria: pass rates and latency thresholds as in the attached spreadsheet.

Attachments (attached to this message):
- Acme_POC_Success_Criteria.xlsx (proposed acceptance thresholds)
- Redwood_Eval_Rubric.pdf (grading rubric + sample template)

Please review the attached rubric  key things you'll see: human grading scale (02), automated metric weightings (50% automated metrics, 50% human grading), and absolute blockers (PII, policy fails). If that weighting looks off to you we can adjust.

Proposed kickoff: Tue 5 Apr 2027 for an internal handoff / evaluation sync. Can you confirm availability?

Thanks,
Marissa
